## Pennsylvania

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/pennsylvania

Pennsylvania does not offer a voluntary defensive-driving program for points reduction or ticket dismissal — PennDOT's Driver Improvement School is mandatory only for drivers who accumulate 6 or more points or are caught speeding 31+ mph over the limit, and completion removes 4 points from the record. For voluntary online courses, the practical benefit is an insurance discount of roughly 5–15% (varies by carrier) rather than any change to your driving record. Ticket dismissal is possible only when a local court approves it on a case-by-case basis, so you must request court permission before enrolling in any course. The Keystone State's approach makes online traffic school useful primarily as an insurance-savings tool, not a points or dismissal mechanism.

The specific municipal court handling your case decides. Rhode Island is a top-10 most expensive state for a speeding ticket once insurance surcharges are factored in, making court dismissal via course completion one of the highest-value defensive driving opportunities in the country when granted.

Approved online courses in Rhode Island run about 6 hours and typically cost $25 to $50. Not available for DUI, reckless driving, or commercial vehicle violations. Individual insurers may offer voluntary discounts for course completion. The return on a $50 course against a $4,000-plus three-year insurance surcharge is roughly 80x when the court grants dismissal.

With court approval, yes. Rhode Island is a top-10 most expensive state for a speeding ticket once insurance surcharges are factored in, so court-granted dismissal via course completion produces one of the highest financial returns available anywhere in the country.

Drivers with a valid RI license and a minor moving violation. Not available for DUI, reckless driving, or commercial vehicle violations. Court permission is required before enrollment.

## Tennessee

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/tennessee

Tennessee drivers convicted of a speeding violation after July 1, 2022 may qualify to remove up to 5 points from their driving record by completing a 4-hour Department of Safety-approved traffic school course, available once every 5 years with a 90-day completion deadline from the date of conviction. The course removes only the points — the conviction itself stays on the record, and the option does not dismiss the ticket; only the issuing court can dismiss. Tennessee also runs a separate 8-hour Defensive Driving Course required when drivers accumulate 12 or more points in any 12-month period (6 for drivers under 18) and receive a notice of proposed suspension; that course is part of the Driver Improvement program, not voluntary points removal. Both tracks are administered by the Tennessee Department of Safety & Homeland Security; both can be taken online when state-approved.

**Does Tennessee traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Yes. With court approval, completing a 4-hour TDOS-approved traffic school course dismisses the ticket — it will not appear on your driving record and no points are assessed. Court must give permission first.

**Can I do Tennessee traffic school online?**
Yes. Tennessee TDOS-approved traffic school courses are available fully online and accepted by courts for ticket dismissal.

**How long is Tennessee traffic school?**
The Tennessee TDOS-approved driver education course (traffic school) is 4 hours. A separate 8-hour defensive driving course also exists for more serious situations and court orders.

**How often can I do Tennessee traffic school?**
For ticket dismissal: no specific state cooldown — court sets rules. For DPS point reduction: once every 4 years. You must complete the course within 90 days of the conviction date to be eligible for point reduction.

**Who submits my certificate in Tennessee?**
Driver submits. You download or receive your certificate by email after completion and submit it to your court by the deadline. Providers do not auto-submit to the court in Tennessee.

## Texas

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/texas

Texas drivers cited for most non-CDL moving violations under 25 mph over the limit can request a TDLR-approved 6-hour Driving Safety Course to dismiss the ticket and keep the conviction off their record, under Code of Criminal Procedure Article 45.0511. The driver must request the court's permission before pleading, plead guilty or no contest, present a valid Texas license and proof of liability insurance, and complete the course within 90 days. Successful completion is reported via certificate to the court and produces a Type 3A driving record entry, which is not a conviction, prevents surcharges and points, and qualifies the driver for a 10% auto-insurance discount for 3 years from many carriers. The dismissal is available once every 12 months per driver, is not available to commercial license holders or for violations 25+ mph over the limit, in construction zones with workers present, or for offenses involving passing a school bus.

**How often can I use Texas defensive driving for ticket dismissal?**
Once per 12 months. You cannot use defensive driving for ticket dismissal if you have already done so within the past 12 months. Additional eligibility: the violation cannot be more than 25 mph over the posted speed limit.

**Can I do Texas defensive driving online?**
Yes. TDLR-approved online defensive driving courses are accepted by all Texas county courts. Always verify your course provider is listed on the TDLR website before enrolling.

**Does Texas defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
Yes — Texas uses deferred disposition. You request it from the court, plead no contest, pay a court fee, complete a 6-hour defensive driving course within 90 days, and the ticket is dismissed entirely from your public record.

**How long is Texas defensive driving?**
Texas requires exactly 6 hours — the shortest state-mandated course length in the country. The course includes 5 hours of instruction plus 1 hour of mandatory breaks.

**Who submits my certificate to the Texas court?**
You do. After completing the course, you receive a certificate and must submit it — along with a copy of your Texas driving record — to the court yourself, by the deadline specified in your deferred disposition order (usually 90 days from the plea date).

## Vermont

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/vermont

Vermont does not currently accept online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal or point reduction. The state's driver improvement programs are in-person only, generally assigned by the DMV rather than voluntarily elected.

Vermont is the cheapest state in America for a first speeding ticket, with an all-in cost of about $1,305 (fine plus three-year insurance surcharge). The relative affordability limits the financial return on any relief mechanism. For a Vermont driver looking at a routine moving violation, the primary options are contesting the ticket at court or accepting the underlying penalty. Online defensive driving isn't a legitimate option in Vermont. Any provider claiming otherwise for VT drivers should be avoided.

**Can I take defensive driving online in Vermont?**
No. Vermont does not accept online defensive driving courses for ticket dismissal or point reduction. Any provider claiming otherwise for Vermont drivers is not offering a legitimate course.

**What driver improvement options does Vermont offer?**
Vermont's driver improvement programs are in-person only, generally assigned by the DMV rather than voluntarily elected.

**Why is Vermont so different from other states on this?**
Vermont is one of a small group of New England states (along with Maine, Massachusetts, and New Hampshire) that does not accept online defensive driving for standard driver relief.

**What are the financial stakes for a Vermont ticket?**
Vermont is the cheapest state in America for a first speeding ticket, with an all-in cost of about $1,305 (fine plus three-year insurance surcharge). The relative affordability limits the financial return on any relief mechanism.

**How can I reduce the insurance impact of a Vermont ticket?**
The primary options are contesting the ticket at court or accepting the underlying penalty. Online defensive driving isn't a legitimate option in Vermont.

## Virginia

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/virginia

Virginia operates a unique two-direction point system administered by the DMV: drivers accumulate demerit points for violations and earn safe driving points for clean years (one per year, capped at five). Voluntarily completing an 8-hour DMV-approved Driver Improvement Clinic credits 5 safe driving points to your record once every 24 months under Va. Code §§46.2-489 and 46.2-498, with the clinic capped at $100. Important caveat: the safe-driving-points credit and the insurance-discount benefit are mutually exclusive — you must declare your purpose at registration and choose one. The DMV-issued Online Driver Improvement Clinic Certificate (Form DIC 552B) is the only document the courts and DMV will accept as proof of completion. Court-ordered clinic attendance — required for drivers who accumulate excessive demerit points or as part of sentencing — must be completed within 90 days or the driver's license will be suspended; the court determines whether safe-driving points are awarded for court-ordered completions. CDL holders cannot receive demerit-point relief through the clinic for offenses committed in commercial vehicles.

**Does Virginia driver improvement dismiss my ticket?**
No. Virginia's Driver Improvement Clinic (DIC) reduces demerit points by 5 points and earns a mandatory insurance discount — but it does not dismiss the ticket or remove the underlying conviction.

**Who submits my certificate in Virginia?**
Your school submits completion to the Virginia DMV, which processes the 5-point reduction automatically. You submit the certificate to your insurance company separately to receive the discount.

**How long is Virginia driver improvement?**
Virginia Driver Improvement Clinic (DIC) courses are 8 hours.

**Can I do Virginia driver improvement online?**
Yes. Virginia DMV-approved online Driver Improvement Clinics are accepted statewide.

**How often can I do Virginia driver improvement?**
Once every 12 months for the demerit point reduction benefit. The auto insurance discount typically lasts 3 years from the date of completion.

**How long is Virginia traffic school?**
Virginia requires 8 hours for a DMV-approved driver improvement course. This is one of the longer requirements in the Southeast, but the course earns you both potential ticket dismissal under deferred disposition and +5 safe driver points on your record.

**Can I do Virginia traffic school online?**
Yes. Virginia DMV-approved online driver improvement courses are available statewide. You can complete the full 8-hour course online at your own pace.

**Does Virginia traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Yes. Virginia courts may offer deferred disposition, allowing ticket dismissal if you complete a DMV-approved driver improvement course. Additionally, completing the course earns +5 positive safe driver points on your Virginia driving record.

---

## Washington

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/washington

Washington does not assess license points or formally dismiss traffic tickets — instead, the state offers ticket deferral, where the court agrees not to report the conviction to the Department of Licensing (DOL) if you complete an approved defensive-driving course. The DOL tracks ticket counts rather than points; 4 moving violations in 12 months or 5 in 24 months triggers license probation, with 2 additional tickets leading to a 30-day suspension. To defer a ticket, you must request court permission before your appearance date, qualify under court-by-court rules (typically a minor moving violation, no other pending citations, no prior deferral within the past 7 years), and complete a 4-hour Level 1 course. The 7-year limit is per driver, not per ticket. Drivers required by the court to take a Level 2 8-hour course — typically habitual or serious violators — fall under a different track that does not produce a deferral. Once-every-7-years availability also applies to license-suspension early-termination via the DOL's safe-driving course path.

**Can I do Washington defensive driving online?**
Yes. Washington-approved online defensive driving courses are available (including from iDriveSafely and others). Ensure your course is approved for Washington deferred finding before enrolling.

**Does Washington defensive driving dismiss my ticket?**
Washington does not dismiss tickets. Instead it offers a deferral — the court does not report the ticket to the DOL, so it does not appear on your driving record or reach your insurer. You must plead no contest and request deferral before your appearance date.

**How often can I use Washington’s deferred finding program?**
Once every 7 years. You may only defer a traffic ticket once in any 7-year period. You must also not have any other citations pending at the time of requesting deferral.

**How long is a Washington defensive driving course?**
The standard Washington Level 1 defensive driving course is 4 hours, designed for most minor moving violations. A Level 2 course is available for more serious violations.

**Who submits my certificate in Washington?**
The driver submits the completion certificate to the court by the deadline the court sets (typically 60 days). Most courts do not grant extensions, so complete the course promptly.

**Can I do Washington traffic school online?**
Yes. Washington DOL-approved online courses are accepted for both Level 1 and Level 2 deferral requirements.

**How long is Washington traffic school?**
Level 1 (first-time minor offenders): 4 hours. Level 2 (habitual or serious violators, court-ordered): 8 hours.

**How often can I do Washington traffic school?**
Once every 7 years. You must not have deferred a ticket within the past 7 years and must not have any other citations pending.

## Washington DC

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/washington-dc

Washington DC operates a limited driver improvement program through the DC Department of Motor Vehicles. The DC Superior Court's Traffic Division has discretion to accept driver improvement course completion in lieu of certain penalties, but this is judge-driven and varies by case. No jurisdiction-wide insurance discount is mandated in DC.

Approved courses generally run about 6 to 8 hours. Course completion may reduce points on the DC driving record when court-approved. For a DC driver looking at a routine moving violation, the insurance surcharge is difficult to prevent through course completion alone. Options include contesting the ticket at DC Superior Court or working with a traffic attorney familiar with DC courts. The defensive driving option is a partial hedge at best.

**Can I take defensive driving online in Washington DC?**
With court approval, sometimes. DC Superior Court's Traffic Division has discretion to accept driver improvement course completion in lieu of certain penalties. Confirm with the specific court before enrolling.

**How long is DC defensive driving?**
Approved courses generally run about 6 to 8 hours.

**How much does DC defensive driving cost?**
Course tuition typically runs $19.95 to $30 for approved online providers.

**Does DC have a state DMV?**
DC handles driver licensing through the DC Department of Motor Vehicles, not a state DMV. Traffic matters are handled through the DC DMV and the DC Superior Court's Traffic Division.

**Will my DC insurance go down after the course?**
No jurisdiction-wide insurance discount is mandated in DC. Individual carriers may offer voluntary discounts for approved course completion; check with your specific insurer before enrolling.

**How can I reduce the insurance impact of a DC ticket?**
For most DC drivers, the strongest path to reducing the insurance impact is contesting the ticket at DC Superior Court, often with the assistance of a traffic attorney familiar with DC courts. Defensive driving is a partial hedge at best.

## Wisconsin

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/wisconsin

Wisconsin drivers can reduce up to 3 demerit points from their driving record by completing a WisDOT-approved Traffic Safety School course, governed by Wis. Admin. Code Trans 101.07. The student has 30 days from completion to notify the DMV to apply the credit, and the option is available only once every 3 years. Wisconsin's demerit point system is built around a rolling 12-month window — only points accumulated in the prior 12 months count toward suspension, with 12+ points triggering a license suspension. If your license is already suspended for accumulating 12 to 14 points, completing the course can lift the suspension. A separate 2-hour Failure to Yield Right-of-Way course is mandatory after a failure-to-yield conviction; it satisfies that specific requirement but does not reduce points. OWI (impaired driving) courses are a separate track entirely.

**Who submits my certificate in Wisconsin?**
For the DMV-mandated Failure to Yield course, your provider submits completion electronically to the Wisconsin DMV. For general traffic school ticket dismissal, you receive a certificate and submit it to your court directly.

**How long is Wisconsin traffic school?**
The Wisconsin Failure to Yield course is 2 hours (state-mandated). General traffic school for ticket dismissal is typically 4 hours, depending on the court's requirements.

**How often can I do Wisconsin traffic school?**
No fixed statewide cooldown for general ticket dismissal — each court sets its own rules. For the DMV-mandated Failure to Yield course, this is a one-time requirement triggered by conviction.

**Can I do Wisconsin traffic school online?**
Yes. Online courses are accepted in Wisconsin for both the Failure to Yield requirement and general traffic school ticket dismissal.

**Does Wisconsin traffic school dismiss my ticket?**
Court-by-court for most violations. The Wisconsin DOT also mandates a specific Failure to Yield course for drivers convicted of that violation. For other minor violations, contact your court to confirm eligibility and get permission before enrolling.

---

## Wyoming

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/wyoming

Wyoming does not use a driver point system — the Wyoming Department of Transportation (WyDOT) tracks moving-violation convictions by count rather than numeric points, and 4 moving-violation convictions within any 12-month period trigger an automatic 90-day license suspension under Title 31 of the Wyoming Statutes. Whether traffic school can dismiss a ticket is decided court-by-court at the circuit court or municipal court level, typically as part of a diversion or deferred-prosecution agreement; some courts approve WyDOT-recognized online defensive driving providers, others do not. CDL holders are generally excluded, as are violations involving 25+ mph over the limit, school zones, accidents, reckless driving, or DUI. Convictions remain on the driving record for 3 years from conviction date. Always contact the issuing court before enrolling in any course — Wyoming has no statewide ticket-dismissal program, and a defensive driving certificate accepted by Laramie Municipal Court may not be accepted by Cheyenne or Casper.

**Does Wyoming have a driver license point system?**
No. Wyoming does not use a numeric driver license point system. Instead, the Wyoming Department of Transportation (WyDOT) tracks the count of moving-violation convictions on a driving record. Four moving-violation convictions within any 12-month period trigger an automatic 90-day license suspension under Title 31 of the Wyoming Statutes; each subsequent violation can extend the suspension by another 90 days.

**Can I take an online defensive driving course to dismiss a Wyoming traffic ticket?**
Sometimes — eligibility depends entirely on which court issued the ticket. Wyoming has no statewide diversion program, so each circuit court and municipal court decides whether to accept a defensive driving completion certificate as a basis for dismissal. Some courts accept WyDOT-recognized online providers; others require an in-person class or do not offer dismissal at all. Contact the court listed on your citation before enrolling.

**Who is not eligible for ticket dismissal through traffic school in Wyoming?**
Most courts that allow traffic-school dismissal exclude commercial driver's license (CDL) holders, drivers cited for speeding 25+ mph over the posted limit, violations in school zones, violations involving accidents, reckless driving, and DUI. The exact exclusion list is set by each court, so confirm with the court that issued your citation.

**How long do traffic violations stay on a Wyoming driving record?**
Traffic conviction records remain on a Wyoming driving record for 3 years from the date of conviction. During that time the conviction can be combined with new violations to trigger the 4-in-12-months suspension threshold, and insurance carriers can typically see the conviction during the rate-setting period.

**Does Wyoming require insurance carriers to give a discount for completing a defensive driving course?**
Wyoming does not statutorily mandate insurance discounts for completing a defensive driving course. Whether your carrier offers a discount, and how much, is up to the individual insurer — contact your auto insurance agent before enrolling if an insurance discount is your primary goal.

**What happens if I get four traffic tickets in 12 months in Wyoming?**
WyDOT will automatically suspend your driver's license for 90 days. The suspension extends by an additional 90 days for each subsequent moving-violation conviction. Because Wyoming uses a violation-count system rather than points, even minor speeding tickets count toward the threshold — there's no equivalent of a low-point violation that doesn't add up.

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/reviews/aceable

**Facts:** Rating 4.8/5 (45,435 reviews on Trustpilot) · from $23.20 · Covers 3 states (CA, TX, FL) · All Courts · 5h course

Aceable is the one traffic school that actually feels built this decade. It started as a mobile app, not a desktop course someone bolted an app onto later, and you can tell. It has north of 45,000 reviews on Trustpilot sitting at 4.8 stars. That's more than any other traffic school we track, and it's not close. If a big pile of happy customers means anything, Aceable has the pile.

The course is built to be fast. It hits your state's minimum required hours and then it stops. No filler modules to run the clock. For most people that's the entire reason they're taking traffic school in the first place, so get in, get done, move on.

You take it on your phone and it's genuinely made for that. Do it in chunks on a lunch break, or sit down and knock the whole thing out in one go. Once you pass, the certificate goes to the court electronically, so there's no mailing anything or waiting on paper. There's a money-back guarantee if it doesn't work out for you.

One thing worth knowing. Aceable only holds its own course license in California and Texas. In a handful of other states, Florida, Ohio, and Oklahoma among them, the course sold under the Aceable name is actually I Drive Safely running underneath. Same course, different label on it. That's not a knock at all. I Drive Safely is one of the oldest and most established schools out there, so you're getting a proven, court-accepted course either way. Just know the experience might feel a little different from the slick app-first version you get in CA and TX.

Price depends on your state, and Aceable isn't trying to be the cheapest option. A few people say the course still feels long even at minimum hours, and a handful flag a total at checkout that wasn't clear up front. So read the full price before you pay.

**Bottom line.** In California or Texas, if you want the smoothest, fastest way through traffic school on your phone, Aceable is the one I'd point you to. That rating isn't luck. And in the states where it's really I Drive Safely under the hood, you're still in good hands, you're just getting it with a different name on the door.

---

## DriversEd.com Review

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/reviews/driversed

**Facts:** Rating 4.6/5 (10,153 reviews on Trustpilot) · from $29.99 · Available nationwide · All Courts · 6h course

[DriversEd.com](http://driversed.com/) has been around since 1998, which in this business is basically forever. It carries more than 10,000 reviews sitting up in the high 4s, so this isn't some fly-by-night operation. If what you want is the safe, established, national name, this is it.

It covers all 50 states, which a lot of schools can't say. The content is thorough and genuinely state-specific, not a generic course with your state's name pasted on the front. The certificate goes to the court electronically, there's a money-back guarantee, and the BBB gives it an A+.

Worth knowing up front: [DriversEd.com](http://driversed.com/) is part of the same family as I Drive Safely, Aceable, and Improv, all one parent company. That's not a problem, it just means if you've used one of those you'll recognize the setup here. You're getting a proven course from a company that's been running these for more than 25 years.

The main knock is price. At around $30 it sits at the higher end, and a few people say the course feels longer than it needs to. You're paying for the brand and the track record more than for speed. If cheapest-possible is the goal, this isn't it. If it's "I want a name I can trust and I don't want to think about it," it's a strong pick.

**Bottom line.** [DriversEd.com](http://driversed.com/) is the dependable, all-50-states option with a long history and a big pile of reviews behind it. You pay a little more for that. For a lot of people, not having to wonder whether the school is legit is worth the extra few dollars.

---

## DriveSafe Online Review

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/reviews/drivesafeonline

**Facts:** Rating 4.8/5 (6,847 reviews on Trustpilot) · from $24.95 · Available nationwide · Most Courts · 6h course

DriveSafe Online is the one that actually tried to make traffic school not miserable. Instead of walls of text you click through half-asleep, the course is built around full-screen video, closer to watching a show than reading a manual. Investopedia named it Best Overall online defensive driving course, and it has a 4.8 on Trustpilot across nearly 7,000 reviews to back that up.

That combination is rare. High volume of reviews and a high score. Plenty of schools have one or the other. DriveSafe Online has both, which tells you the video-first approach actually lands with people.

The practical stuff is clean. Electronic certificate, a money-back guarantee if the court won't accept it, and no hidden fees, which given the upsell games some competitors play is worth something on its own. Price sits around $25, right in the fair-value middle.

Two things to check before you buy. It isn't in all 50 states, so confirm yours is covered. And the course length varies by state, so your time commitment depends on where you are. One specific heads-up: in Arizona this is an insurance-discount course, not a ticket-dismissal one, so Arizona drivers trying to get a ticket off their record should look elsewhere.

**Bottom line.** If you'd rather watch your way through traffic school than read your way through it, and you want a school with genuinely strong independent reviews, DriveSafe Online is the one I'd start with. Just confirm it covers your state first.

---

## GoToTrafficSchool Review

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/reviews/gototrafficschool

**Facts:** Rating 3.1/5 (233 reviews on Trustpilot) · from $19.95 · Covers 46 states (AL, AK, AZ, AR, CA, CO, CT, DE, FL, GA, HI, ID, IL, IN, IA, KS, LA, ME, MD, MA, MN, MS, MO, MT, NE, NV, NH, NJ, NM, NY, NC, OK, OR, PA, RI, SC, SD, TN, TX, UT, VT, VA, WA, WV, WI, WY) · Most Courts · 4h course

GoToTrafficSchool plays one game and plays it hard: price. It runs a lowest-price guarantee, so if you find a cheaper approved course they'll beat it. There's even a pay-later setup where you take the whole course first and only pay at the final exam. If your budget is the whole decision, that's hard to argue with.

It's not new, either. The company's been at this since 2000 and claims more than 6 million drivers served, with an A+ from the BBB. It's approved in almost every state, so coverage isn't the problem.

Here's the honest part. Its Trustpilot rating is low, low enough that I'm not going to dress it up. The reviews it does have are thin, and the complaints tend to cluster on the same thing: upsells. The base price is cheap, but expect to get nudged toward paid add-ons like a read-along audio option or same-day certificate delivery. So the sticker price and the checkout total aren't always the same number.

None of that makes it a scam. Millions of people have gotten their certificate through it and moved on. It's a get-it-done, no-frills course, and the experience matches the price. You're not buying polish here.

**Bottom line.** If the cheapest legit option is what you're after, and you don't mind saying no to a few upsells on the way through, GoToTrafficSchool does the job and the price guarantee is real. If you want a smooth, premium experience, spend a little more somewhere else.

## Traffic School Online Review

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/reviews/trafficschoolonline

**Facts:** Rating 4.7/5 (7,874 reviews on Trustpilot) · from $29.97 · Available nationwide · All Courts · 4h course

Traffic School Online has quietly built one of the better review records in the category: a 4.7 on Trustpilot across more than 7,500 reviews. That's a lot of people, and a high score to hold across that many. When both numbers are strong, it usually means the thing just works.

It's approved across the states it covers, and electronic submission to your court or DMV is included, so once you finish, the paperwork mostly handles itself. There's a money-back guarantee, and its customer support reputation is one of the stronger ones here. That matters more than people think, right up until you're stuck on a Sunday needing your certificate.

Where it's light is coverage and format. It doesn't blanket all 50 states the way DriversEd does, so check that yours is on the list. And there's no dedicated mobile app, so if doing the whole thing from a polished phone app is your dealbreaker, this isn't the one. You can still take it in a phone browser, it's just not app-first like Aceable.

**Bottom line.** Traffic School Online is a quietly reliable pick with a strong review track record and support that actually shows up. If it covers your state and you don't need a native app, it's an easy one to recommend.

---

## Improv Traffic School Review

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/reviews/improv

**Facts:** Rating 4.3/5 (1,469 reviews on Trustpilot) · from $24.95 · Covers 37 states (CA, FL, TX, AZ, NJ, IN, MO, NV, TN, VA, GA, IL, AL, AK, AR, CT, DE, ID, IA, KS, MD, MN, MS, MT, NE, NH, NM, NY, ND, OR, PA, SC, SD, UT, WA, WV, WI) · Most Courts · 6h course

Improv's whole angle is that traffic school doesn't have to be boring. The course is built around comedy, so instead of a dry lecture you get the material with jokes woven through. If the thing you dread about traffic school is the tedium, that's a real selling point, and it's where the name comes from.

It carries a rating in the mid-4s across more than 1,400 reviews, and it's affiliated with GEICO, which is a decent trust signal. Certificate goes in electronically, there's a money-back guarantee, and the price is competitive at around $25.

Worth knowing: Improv is part of the same family as Aceable, [DriversEd.com](http://driversed.com/), and I Drive Safely, all one parent company. So under the comedy wrapper it's a well-established operation, not a novelty act. The catch is coverage. It's really built for California, Florida, Texas, and Arizona, so if you're outside those, check before you count on it.

The reviews that complain tend to hit customer service and the odd clunky moment in the flow, so it's not flawless. But the core promise, a course that's actually watchable, mostly holds up.

**Bottom line.** If you're in CA, FL, TX, or AZ and a funny traffic school sounds better than a boring one, Improv is worth the look. Just confirm it covers your state, and go in knowing the comedy is the point.

## TicketSchool Review

**URL:** https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/reviews/ticketschool

**Facts:** Rating 4.7/5 (432 reviews on Trustpilot) · from $19.95 · Covers 3 states (CA, FL, TX) · Most Courts · 4h course

TicketSchool is the no-fuss, competitively priced option for drivers in California, Florida, and Texas. At $19.95 it's priced with the cheap crowd, but it carries a 4.7 on Trustpilot, which is a better rating than most of the budget names manage. It's been around since 2005, so it's not new.

The pitch is simple. Court-approved where it operates, fast to get through, and quick on the certificate once you're done. The reviews it has are positive and hit the usual notes, easy to complete, fast turnaround. Electronic certificate, money-back guarantee, the standard boxes are checked.

The honest limit is social proof. It has only a few hundred reviews, which is thin next to schools sitting on thousands. That doesn't make it worse. Plenty of good small operators just haven't collected reviews at scale. But if a giant wall of ratings is what makes you comfortable hitting buy, TicketSchool won't give you that. And it only covers California, Florida, and Texas, so outside those three it isn't an option.

**Bottom line.** If you're in CA, FL, or TX and you want a cheap, court-approved course that gets you in and out without drama, TicketSchool is a fair pick. Just know you're trusting a smaller name with a thinner review pile in exchange for the low price.

## The True Cost of a Traffic Ticket (2026 study)

> TrafficSchoolPicker analysis of all 51 US jurisdictions. All-in cost of a first speeding ticket
> = fine + estimated 3-year insurance surcharge. Full write-up:
> https://www.trafficschoolpicker.com/blog/true-cost-of-a-traffic-ticket

- Nationally, one speeding ticket costs about $435 more per year in insurance (~$1,300 over 3 years). The average 24-25% rate increase dwarfs the ~$130 average 10-over fine.
- Most expensive states, all-in: Michigan $8,742, California $5,619, Hawaii $5,227, Texas $5,047, New Jersey $4,965, Delaware $4,582, Louisiana $4,512, Rhode Island $4,481, Nevada $4,228, Florida $4,170.
- Cheapest states, all-in: Vermont $1,305, Montana $1,486, Pennsylvania $1,494, Nebraska $1,528, Ohio $1,684, Utah $1,792, Virginia $1,818, Maryland $1,869, New Hampshire $2,024, Maine $2,100.
- Biggest traffic-school net savings: Michigan ~$8,600, California ~$5,300, Hawaii ~$5,050, Texas ~$4,650, Louisiana ~$4,300, Nevada ~$3,950, Florida ~$3,900, Tennessee ~$2,950, Arizona ~$2,950, Oklahoma ~$2,350.
- Texas example: a driving-safety-course dismissal (~$182 all-in incl. court fee + driving record) prevents ~$4,800 in 3-year surcharges, ~26x return. Mechanism is dismissal, not a discount.
- Course mechanisms differ by state: masking (CA, VC §1808.7), dismissal (TX, Art. 45A.352), adjudication withheld (FL, §318.14), base-rate discount (NY PIRP, insurers still see the ticket), one-time point masking (MI BDIC). PA/MA/NJ/KS offer little for a first ticket.
- Sources: FinanceBuzz (fines), CarInsurance.com/Quadrant (surcharges), U.S. News, NHTSA. Rankings are source-dependent (esp. Hawaii).
